data.title: Crude oil extends the rebound as growth concerns ease and US-Iran tensions provide support
data.description:
Crude oil has been rallying steadily since Wednesday as growth concerns reached a near-term peak. Keep in mind that growth fears could still push oil prices lower in the future, but we will likely need a bigger selloff in the stock market, an even more hawkish Fed or weak economic data to increase the bearish momentum.

On the news front, Trump touted the US naval blockade and continued military deployment while saying that Washington is still giving Iran an opportunity to reach an agreement. He also threatened to strike Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain if no deal is reached.

data.title: Ethereum consolidates near yearly lows as bearish macro backdrop remains intact despite short-covering
data.description:
Ethereum is also consolidating near yearly lows as the macro backdrop remains negative for the crypto market. There’s been some broad short-covering, but no positive catalyst backing the move.

Keep in mind that cryptocurrencies are particularly sensitive to changes in liquidity and risk sentiment, so higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions tend to be strong bearish drivers.

data.title: Gold extends gains after a key technical breakout as broad short-covering improves sentiment
data.description:
Gold extended the rebound during the Asian session after a key technical breakout, despite no catalyst backing the move. Given a similar price action across many other markets, it looks more like broad short-covering as growth concerns reached a near-term peak.  

Traders continue to wait for fresh catalysts, with attention now turning to the FOMC decision in two weeks and the next set of key US data. The US-Iran developments will also be in focus of course, as an escalation could trigger a surge in oil prices, while a breakthrough would drastically improve future growth expectations.

data.title: Spanish inflation comes off the boil in November, offering some respite for the ECB
data.description:
• Spain November preliminary CPI +4.1% vs +4.6% y/y expected
  • Prior +4.9%
  • Spain November preliminary HICP +4.1% vs +4.7% y/y expected
  • Prior +4.9%

Much like the French report earlier, Spain's inflation numbers are also seen cooling off in November. After nearly hitting 5% in October, headline annual inflation is seen dropping back to 4.1% this month. The added good news is that core annual inflation was also estimated to drop to 2.6% in November, as compared to the 3.1% reading in the month before.

data.description:
• France Q3 final GDP -0.2% vs -0.1% q/q prelim
  • Prior 0.0%

Ouch. France was already the troubling spot in the euro area and the negative revision to the preliminary GDP estimates only continues to underscore that notion. In volume terms, the French economy contracted by 0.2% in Q3 following some tentative stability in the previous quarter.

data.title: France inflation undershoots estimates in November as energy and services price pressures ease
data.description:
• France November preliminary CPI +2.9% vs +3.2% y/y expected
  • Prior +3.4%
  • France November preliminary HICP +3.2% vs +3.6% y/y expected
  • Prior +3.7%

Well, that's some good news for the French economy as inflation pressures are seen cooling back a little in November. The drop here is even below analyst estimates, with headline annual inflation dropping back below 3%. The monthly reading also shows that French inflation should ease by 0.7% in November, after having risen by 0.4% in October.

data.title: What are the main events for today?
data.description:
EUROPEAN SESSION

In the European session, we get the preliminary inflation reports from France and Spain. The French HICP Y/Y is expected at 3.6% vs 3.7% prior, while the Spanish HICP Y/Y is seen at 4.7% vs 4.9% prior. Headline inflation is expected to ease for everyone in November after the big commodities' selloff, so this wouldn't be a surprise at all. 

The data is unlikely to change much at this point as the market is already fully expecting an ECB rate hike in December and another one in June 2027. Moreover, oil prices have been rising pretty quickly since Wednesday as the easing in growth concerns and the prolonged US-Iran stalemate provided a tailwind. Therefore, I wouldn't focus on headline inflation in November, but more on core inflation.

data.title: US reportedly urged Venezuela, Iraq to consider quitting OPEC earlier this year
data.description:
US president Trump has never been much of a fan of OPEC. And as it would seem, he'd quite like a few of its members to feel the same way.

In an exclusive report by Reuters today, the US administration is said to have encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to contemplate leaving OPEC earlier this year. Washington reportedly even blocked Venezuela's annual membership payment, while Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman intervened over the summer to persuade the US to back off.

data.title: XBTFX Expands Partner Programs With Lifetime IB Rebates and CPA Payouts Up to $1,850
data.description:
Building an audience in financial markets takes time, and building sustainable revenue from that audience can be even more challenging.

data.title: Reminder: Wall Street is back today but will dip buyers have the last laugh?
data.description:
It looks like dip buyers are coming back from their Thanksgiving dinner with quite the appetite. US futures are storming higher so far today, with S&P 500 futures up 1.8% and Nasdaq futures up a whopping 2.8% as tech shares look to end a bruising week on a brighter note.

After the impressive turnaround on Wednesday, there is a growing sense of optimism that dip buyers might finally be getting somewhere. However, the key question to end the week is whether they keep the party going when Wall Street returns later today?

data.title: Gold begins to find its feet again but are buyers out of the woods yet?
data.description:
Gold buyers have at least something to be thankful for this week. After a rather brutal month as a whole, the precious metal is finding a bit of a reprieve today as it pushes back above $3,600.

The question now though is how much should we really read into the latest bounce over the past few sessions?
